en: The hottest time of day is usually around 3 PM, not noon, because Earth's surface needs time to absorb and re-radiate the Sun's energy.
Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by how far Earth is from the Sun during its orbit.
Moon phases are caused by changing angles of sunlight hitting the Moon as it orbits Earth, not by Earth's shadow falling on the Moon.
Lightning strikes the same place many times; the Empire State Building in New York is hit by lightning about 25 times every year.
Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale, rated 1, and can be easily scratched by a human fingernail.
Healthy soil is made of broken-down rock, organic matter called humus, water, air, and living organisms like earthworms and bacteria.
Only about 2.5 percent of all water on Earth is freshwater, and most of that freshwater is frozen in glaciers and ice caps.
Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
The Sun is a medium-sized star; the red supergiant star UY Scuti has a radius roughly 1,700 times larger than the Sun.
Earthquakes start at a point called the focus deep underground, sometimes hundreds of kilometers below Earth's surface, not just at ground level.
Some volcanoes like Mount Pinatubo erupt explosively with ash and gas instead of flowing lava, because thick magma traps pressure underground.
The Moon does not produce its own light; the bright glow we see at night is sunlight reflected off the Moon's rocky surface.
